n0001.title: GPT-3 and the Scaling Hypothesis
n0001.gist: GPT-3's unexpected meta-learning and unbroken scaling curves vindicate the scaling hypothesis, showing that larger models trained on more data yield qualitative leaps and challenge AI risk critics.

n0002.title: The Deep Learning Revolution Begins
n0002.gist: The author frames GPT-3 as evidence that neural nets absorb data and compute, becoming more Bayesian and manifesting new abilities as problems get harder.

n0005.title: Meta-Learning and Flexing GPT
n0005.gist: GPT-3's release demonstrated meta-learning and creative flexing beyond standard benchmarks, showing it can learn new tasks from a few examples.

n0006.title: Meta-Learning
n0006.gist: GPT-3 was released quietly and showed it can solve arithmetic, translation, anagrams, and SAT analogies purely from prompted examples, implying its attention mechanisms learned to learn.

n0009.title: Flexing GPT
n0009.gist: GPT-3 is a 'magnificently obsolete' architecture that nevertheless manifests crazy runtime meta-learning and creative outputs not captured by standard NLP benchmarks.

n0014.title: Baking the Cake and Scaling
n0014.gist: GPT-3 is not whole AGI but a big part, and its continued scaling follows predictable logarithmic curves with plenty of room for further improvement.

n0015.title: Baking The Cake
n0015.gist: GPT-3 is not whole AGI but a big part, and its cost is trivial by scientific budgets despite anti-scaling objections.

n0023.title: Scaling
n0023.gist: The scaling laws hold for GPT-3 and leave plenty of room for further loss decreases, suggesting future models will continue to improve predictably.

n0032.title: Blessings of Scale and Hypothesis
n0032.gist: Deep learning enjoys blessings of scale where hard problems become easier as models grow, supporting the scaling hypothesis that intelligence emerges from simple architectures at sufficient scale.

n0033.title: Blessings Of Scale
n0033.gist: Training large models on hard, varied problems makes them more stable, generalizable, and capable of meta-learning because they function as ensembles of sub-models that average to Occam's razor.

n0046.title: Scaling Hypothesis
n0046.gist: The strong scaling hypothesis claims that ever larger NNs trained on diverse data will naturally produce ever more sophisticated behavior, and the author admits the advocates were right.

n0050.title: Why Does Pretraining Work?
n0050.gist: The pretraining thesis argues that minimizing next-token prediction loss on human-generated data forces models to learn increasingly deep linguistic and cognitive structures, with the final bits requiring true intelligence.

n0051.title: The Pretraining Thesis
n0051.gist: Humans emit structured data, and a model that predicts all of it must learn logic, causality, and reasoning to solve the long tail.

n0056.title: From Gibberish to Sentences
n0056.gist: Language models progress from letter frequencies to words, syntax, and long-range coherence as training loss decreases, each stage requiring more data and compute.

n0065.title: The Last Bits Are Deepest
n0065.gist: The final bits of prediction error require true understanding, and human-level language modeling would imply replacement of humans in text-writing jobs.

n0074.title: Reasons for Doubt
n0074.gist: The pretraining thesis felt like a magic trick, with possible barriers including insufficient data, saturation, or architectural limits, but apparently scaling would have worked fine.

n0079.title: Open Questions About Future Models
n0079.gist: Nobody predicted quantitatively the capabilities at GPT-3's scale, and nobody knows what a further drop in loss to 1.24 or below would gain.

n0086.title: Prospects and Critiquing the Critics
n0086.gist: OA's startup-like bet on scaling will likely pay off because competitors lack conviction, while experts' phatic, non-predictive criticism has consistently failed and exemplifies bureaucratic authority without accountability.

n0087.title: Prospects
n0087.gist: OA's startup-like bet on scaling will likely pay off because competitors lack conviction and a hardware overhang means the limiting factor is human vision rather than compute.

n0100.title: Critiquing The Critics
n0100.gist: The experts' phatic, non-predictive criticism has consistently failed to foresee deep learning's success, and their authority without accountability is an iron law of bureaucracy.

n0116.title: Appendix: It From Byte
n0116.gist: The appendix first argues that agency is a continuum useful for non-agentic systems, and inducing it may be expensive but possible.

n0117.title: Appendix
n0117.gist: The appendix begins by situating the argument that agency may emerge from non-agentic data.

n0119.title: It From Byte
n0119.gist: GPT-3 learns from human data to imitate agents, and agency is not discrete but a continuum that may emerge from many non-agentic problems at scale.

n0127.title: All Is Atoms & Void
n0127.gist: Since agency is built from non-agentic atoms, there is no principled distinction between agentic and natural data, and physics simulations could in principle recapitulate agents.

n0131.title: Intentional Interpretive Stance
n0131.gist: Humans use Dennett's intentional stance to model natural systems as agents, and this shortcut is predictively useful and mathematically equivalent to step-by-step physics.

n0134.title: Variational Interpretations
n0134.gist: The author embraces Janus's description of GPT-3 as physics-like world-modeler and argues that variational principles are a universal trick neural nets would naturally adopt.

n0141.title: Inducing Emergence Is Expensive
n0141.gist: Variational agency is powerful but expensive to learn, requiring rich models, enough data, and training to force out simpler solutions.

n0144.title: What Can Induce Agency Emergence?
n0144.gist: Whether Pluto-like systems or exoplanets induce agency is an empirical question, and we cannot say a priori what scale or diversity of data will bring it about.

n0147.title: Agency in Simple Systems
n0147.gist: Even abstract systems like cellular automata and Turing machines may induce agency, because meta-learning over many Turing machines could require inferring rules and goals.

n0148.title: Cellular Automatons
n0148.gist: Game of Life patterns like gliders can be chunked as entities, leading to an intentional stance even in simple cellular automata.

n0154.title: Turing Machine
n0154.gist: Considering all Turing machines with random programs as sequence prediction, the original formulation even includes a homunculus that follows instructions.

n0157.title: Single TM
n0157.gist: A single random Turing machine likely does not induce agency because it has no maximizing behavior, but it may foster instruction-following.

n0161.title: TM Meta-Learning
n0161.gist: Training over many Turing machines may force inferring rules and goals, resembling rudimentary theory of mind and making agency hard to avoid.

n0166.title: Ambient Agency
n0166.gist: Agency may be like Turing-completeness: too useful and convergent to guarantee absence, so tool AIs may inevitably become agent AIs as they improve.
